title: Merge Intervals
description: Given a list of `[start, end]` intervals in any order, merge every group of overlapping intervals and return the non-overlapping intervals that cover exactly the same ranges, sorted by start. Intervals that merely touch at an endpoint, like `[1,2]` and `[2,3]`, count as overlapping.
hints: The input is unsorted. What ordering would make overlapping intervals neighbours?
After sorting by start, an interval can only overlap the most recently built merged interval.
Keep an output list. If the next start is <= the last output end, extend that end with a max; otherwise append a new interval.
starterCode:
class Solution:
    def merge(self, intervals: List[List[int]]) -> List[List[int]]:

solution.explanation: Sort the intervals by start. Then sweep through them, keeping a result list: if the current interval starts at or before the end of the last result interval they overlap, so set that end to the max of the two ends; otherwise append the current interval as a new group. Sorting dominates, giving O(n log n) time, with O(n) space for the output.
